what: The Quick Access panel's frame rate while an answer streams in, what was costing it, and the two fixes (plan 69, the maintainer's ask: 'it should be 60, 45 min').
device: Steam Deck, Quick Access Menu on the external monitor, no game running, model gemma4:e2b-it-qat on the graphics chip, answers with thinking on.

method.frame_rate: requestAnimationFrame callbacks per second in the Quick Access page, over alternating segments of 2.5 s inside ONE streaming answer (first 0.3 s of each segment dropped), so every comparison shares the same answer and model load. Single segments vary by about +-5 frames a second; compare pairs, not single numbers.
method.switches: Test builds only (never committed): window.__bonsaiRevealStepMs (reveal and scramble on a shared timer grid instead of every frame), window.__bonsaiStreamPollMs (text arrival rate), window.__bonsaiScrambleOff. Glows paused through the page's own Animation objects. Stylesheet variants injected with CSS.createStyleSheet and removed after.
method.real_changes: Frames that followed a DOM mutation inside the panel, with attribute writes that left the value unchanged filtered out (imperfectly: a set-and-reset inside one task still counts once).
method.probes: Scratchpad scripts probe_step_ab.py .. probe_step_ab7.py and probe_beat_check.py, run on the Deck over ssh; not kept in the repo.

findings.question: Is the model sharing the graphics chip the limit by itself?
findings.answer: No. During the thinking phase (model generating, thinking box changing 6-7 times a second, glows running) the panel held 59-60 frames a second.

findings.question: How much does moving the answer's text on every frame cost?
findings.answer: Most of it. With the text and scramble stepping on a 110 ms grid instead of every frame, the panel roughly doubled its frame rate.

findings.question: Ruled out on the way
findings.answer: Slowing the model's text arrivals from 7 to 2 a second (41.9 / 39.1 vs 42.7 / 38.4): no gain. Giving the chat's scroller its own layer (44.1 / 39.2 vs 41.2 / 43.3): no gain; the chat scrolls under once a second during an answer. In the small hours of the same day: pausing all animations, removing the blur, and switching off the 38 contains rules each made no difference while the text still moved every frame.

findings.question: Why did the scramble cost extra even on the grid?
findings.answer: Its own reshuffle timer and its markdown step landed in frames of their own, so each beat cost two or three redraws (about 20 changed frames a second at a 9-a-second beat). Fixed in bb8d7e5b: the reveal's render takes the scramble's beat in the same commit; after it, about 13 changed frames a second, and hiding the symbols' drawing made little difference (50.7 / 47.2 / 47.2 drawn vs 54.0 / 48.1 / 47.3 not drawn).

findings.question: What do the two glows cost?
findings.answer: About 5 frames a second while an answer streams (the bubble's box-shadow pulse and the question box's breathing each redraw every frame), nothing while thinking. Fixed in aae5add6: both hold steady while the answer's text arrives.

animations_running_during_answer: bonsai-caret-blink (the question box's cursor, two changes a second)

not_measured: With a game running (the plan's own frame-rate rows use Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor); the Deck's own screen; the game's own frame rate.
side_notes: Every root render rewrites the question box input's name and type attributes and the Decky pane's class to the same values (Steam's own components); harmless to the frame rate as far as measured, but it makes naive change counters over-count.
The Deck's screensaver came on once between runs; a controller press cleared it.
